questions.memo: Overcrowded slides overwhelm the audience. A clear layout with key points and readable visuals communicates far better.

questions.question: Why is combining verbal and non-verbal formats often the most effective presentation?
options: The spoken words explain, while visuals make the information clearer and more memorable
Two formats always confuse the audience
Words and visuals cannot be used together
questions.expected: The spoken words explain, while visuals make the information clearer and more memorable
questions.memo: Words give the explanation and visuals make patterns clear and memorable, so using both together reaches the audience best.

questions.question: Two presenters share the same data. One opens with the key finding and a clear graph; the other buries it on the last slide. Which is more effective, and why?
options: The first, because leading with the key point and a clear visual makes the message land
The second, because hiding the point builds suspense
They are equally effective regardless of order
questions.expected: The first, because leading with the key point and a clear visual makes the message land
questions.memo: Putting the most important information first, supported by a clear visual, ensures the audience grasps the key message.

questions.question: Sort each statement as TRUE or FALSE about presenting information.

items.text: A graph is a non-verbal presentation
Visual aids support the spoken words
Good presentations hide the main point
A clear layout uses headings and short points
Crowded, tiny text helps the audience

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Verbal = words, non-verbal = visuals; aids support the talk; and good layout leads with the key point in a clear, readable way.

BUS.G10.T3.BUSPLAN.A1.title: The business plan
BUS.G10.T3.BUSPLAN.A1.description: The purpose and components of a business plan — cover page, executive summary, business description, vision/mission, ownership, product/service, legal requirements, SWOT and the marketing plan (market research and the marketing mix, the 4 or 7 Ps) — and the job each part does.
BUS.G10.T3.BUSPLAN.A1.strand: T3 — Creative thinking, opportunity, location, contracts, presentation & the business plan
BUS.G10.T3.BUSPLAN.A1.recovery_strategy: A business plan proves the venture is viable. Know each component's job: executive summary = short overview; marketing plan = how you reach customers (the Ps); financial analysis = does it make money.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a business plan?
options: To show that the venture is viable and plan how it will work
To replace the need for any customers
questions.expected: To show that the venture is viable and plan how it will work
questions.memo: A business plan sets out how the business will work and shows that the venture can succeed (is viable).

questions.question: True or false: The executive summary gives a short overview of the whole business plan.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: The executive summary is a short overview of the key points, so a reader grasps the plan quickly.

questions.question: The _________ plan explains how the business will reach and sell to its customers.
questions.expected: marketing
questions.memo: The marketing plan covers market research and the marketing mix — how the business will reach and sell to customers.

questions.question: Which of these is a component of a business plan?
questions.expected: The executive summary
questions.memo: The executive summary is a real component of a business plan. The others have nothing to do with it.

questions.question: True or false: A business plan usually includes a SWOT analysis.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: A SWOT analysis is part of a business plan — it weighs the venture's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats.

questions.question: The 4 Ps of the marketing mix are product, price, place and _________.
questions.expected: promotion
questions.memo: The 4 Ps are product, price, place and promotion. (The 7 Ps add people, process and physical evidence.)

questions.question: What does the executive summary of a business plan contain?
options: A short overview of the key points of the whole plan
A list of competitors' phone numbers
questions.expected: A short overview of the key points of the whole plan
questions.memo: The executive summary is a brief overview of the main points — not personal details or raw data.

questions.question: What does the marketing plan section cover?
options: Market research and the marketing mix (the Ps)
questions.expected: Market research and the marketing mix (the Ps)
questions.memo: The marketing plan sets out market research and the marketing mix — how the business will reach customers.

questions.question: Match each component of a business plan to the job it does.

items.text: Gives a short overview of the whole plan
Shows how the business will reach customers
Shows whether the business will make a profit
The key points an investor reads first
Covers product, price, place and promotion
Sets out the expected income and costs

questions.expected: All six matched to the correct component (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Executive summary = short overview; marketing plan = how to reach customers (the Ps); financial plan = does it make money.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the financial section of a business plan?
options: To show whether the business will make enough money to be viable
questions.expected: To show whether the business will make enough money to be viable
questions.memo: The financial section shows expected income, costs and profit — proving the venture can pay its way.

questions.question: The cover page of a business plan shows the business's _________ and contact details.
questions.expected: name
questions.memo: The cover page carries the business's name and contact details — the first thing the reader sees.

questions.question: Which option shows the usual order of the main parts of a business plan?
options: Cover page → executive summary → business description → marketing plan → financial plan
Financial plan → marketing plan → business description → executive summary → cover page
Marketing plan → cover page → financial plan → business description → executive summary
Business description → financial plan → cover page → marketing plan → executive summary
questions.expected: Cover page → executive summary → business description → marketing plan → financial plan
questions.memo: A plan opens with the cover page and executive summary, then describes the business, then the marketing plan, and ends with the financial plan.

questions.question: Why does a business plan include a section on legal requirements?
options: To show the business will operate within the law (licences, registration, regulations)
To list the owner's favourite laws
questions.expected: To show the business will operate within the law (licences, registration, regulations)
questions.memo: The legal section shows the business knows and will meet its legal duties — licences, registration and regulations.

questions.question: True or false: The executive summary should list the owner's personal hobbies.
questions.expected: False
questions.memo: False — the executive summary gives a short overview of the plan's key points, not personal hobbies.

questions.question: Which three Ps do the 7 Ps add to the original 4 Ps?
questions.expected: People, process and physical evidence
questions.memo: The 7 Ps add people, process and physical evidence to the original product, price, place and promotion.

questions.question: Sort each item as part of the marketing mix (a 'P') or not part of it.

buckets.label: Not part of the marketing mix

questions.expected: All six items sorted correctly (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: The marketing mix is the Ps: product, price, place, promotion (and more). The owner's food and the weather are not part of it.

questions.question: An entrepreneur shows investors a business plan with no financial section. What is the main risk?
options: Investors cannot see whether the business will make money, so they are unlikely to back it
The plan is automatically perfect without it
It makes no difference to investors
It guarantees the business will succeed
questions.expected: Investors cannot see whether the business will make money, so they are unlikely to back it
questions.memo: Without a financial section, no one can judge whether the venture is viable — so investors will not risk their money.

questions.question: Why is a SWOT analysis useful inside a business plan?
options: It honestly weighs the venture's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats so readers can judge its chances
It replaces the marketing plan entirely
questions.expected: It honestly weighs the venture's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats so readers can judge its chances
questions.memo: A SWOT shows the plan has honestly assessed the venture's internal and external position, helping readers judge whether it is viable.

questions.question: A busy investor has only two minutes and wants the gist of the whole venture. Which component should she read?
options: The executive summary, because it is the short overview of the whole plan
questions.expected: The executive summary, because it is the short overview of the whole plan
questions.memo: The executive summary exists exactly for this: a quick overview so a busy reader gets the key points fast.

questions.question: Match each piece of content to the business-plan component it belongs in.

items.text: A one-page summary for a busy investor
A plan for advertising and pricing
A forecast of profit and cash flow
A quick overview of the whole venture
Details of the target market and the Ps

questions.expected: All six pieces matched to the right component (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Overviews go in the executive summary; reaching customers and the Ps go in the marketing plan; income, costs and profit go in the financial plan.

BUS.G10.T4.SELFMAN.A1.title: Self-management
BUS.G10.T4.SELFMAN.A1.description: The concept of self-management and its place in business — time management, personal goals, a balanced lifestyle, a professional image, self-knowledge, self-confidence, stress management and adaptability — kept apart from being managed by others.
BUS.G10.T4.SELFMAN.A1.recovery_strategy: Self-management = managing yourself: your time, goals, image and stress, without being told. It is the foundation for managing others later.

questions.question: What is self-management?
options: Managing your own time, goals and behaviour without being told
Waiting for a boss to control everything you do
Managing other people's work for them
questions.expected: Managing your own time, goals and behaviour without being told
questions.memo: Self-management means taking charge of yourself — your time, goals and behaviour — without needing to be told.

questions.question: True or false: Time management is part of self-management.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Managing your own time well is a core part of self-management.

questions.question: Managing how you use your hours each day is called _________ management.
questions.expected: time
questions.memo: Time management is planning and using your hours well so you get your work done.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of self-management?
options: Setting your own goals and meeting your deadlines
Waiting to be told to start every task
Letting others plan your whole day
questions.expected: Setting your own goals and meeting your deadlines
questions.memo: Setting goals and meeting deadlines on your own is self-management in action.

questions.question: True or false: Self-management means waiting for your supervisor to tell you what to do.
questions.expected: False
questions.memo: False — that is being managed by others. Self-management is taking charge of yourself without being told.

questions.question: Keeping a healthy balance between work, rest and personal life is having a balanced _________.
questions.expected: lifestyle
questions.memo: A balanced lifestyle — mixing work with rest and personal time — is part of managing yourself well.

questions.question: A worker plans her own day, prioritises her tasks and meets deadlines without being reminded. What is she showing?
options: A need to be controlled by others
questions.expected: Good self-management
questions.memo: Planning, prioritising and meeting deadlines on her own is exactly what good self-management looks like.

questions.question: What does developing a professional image mean?
options: Dressing and behaving appropriately so people take you seriously at work
Wearing whatever you like, however untidy
questions.expected: Dressing and behaving appropriately so people take you seriously at work
questions.memo: A professional image is about how you present yourself — dressing and behaving in a way that earns respect at work.

questions.question: Sort each action as self-management or being managed by others.

items.text: Needing a supervisor to check every step

questions.expected: All six actions sorted correctly (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Self-management is acting on your own (planning, goal-setting, meeting deadlines). Being managed by others is waiting to be told at every step.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of stress management?
options: Taking a short break and breathing slowly before a big task
Bottling everything up until you explode
questions.expected: Taking a short break and breathing slowly before a big task
questions.memo: Stress management means using healthy ways — breaks, breathing, exercise — to stay calm and cope with pressure.

questions.question: Build an explanation of why self-management matters in business.
questions.prompt: Pick the best option for each slot to explain why self-management matters.

options.text: Self-management means taking charge of your own time, goals and behaviour
Self-management means waiting for others to manage you
Self-management means avoiding all work
A self-managed person plans their day, meets deadlines and stays professional without being told
A self-managed person only acts when a supervisor gives an instruction
A self-managed person ignores their goals and deadlines
This makes them reliable and productive and prepares them to manage others later
This means they can never work in a team
This is exactly the same as being controlled by others

questions.memo: Claim: self-management is taking charge of yourself. Evidence: planning, meeting deadlines, staying professional without being told. Explanation: it makes you reliable and ready to manage others.

questions.question: Knowing your own strengths and weaknesses honestly is called self-_________.
questions.expected: knowledge
questions.memo: Self-knowledge is understanding your own strengths and weaknesses, so you can build on them and improve.

questions.question: How does adaptability show good self-management?
options: You stay calm and adjust your plans when things change
You refuse to change anything ever
You panic and give up when plans change
You wait for someone else to fix everything
questions.expected: You stay calm and adjust your plans when things change
questions.memo: Adaptability is adjusting calmly to change — a key self-management skill when plans don't go as expected.

questions.question: True or false: Self-confidence helps a person take on tasks and bounce back from setbacks.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Self-confidence — believing in your own ability — helps you take on challenges and recover from setbacks.

questions.question: Which of these shows POOR self-management?
options: Leaving every task to the last minute and missing deadlines
questions.expected: Leaving every task to the last minute and missing deadlines
questions.memo: Procrastinating and missing deadlines is poor self-management. The others are all good self-management habits.

questions.question: Sort each habit as good or poor self-management.

items.text: Leaving everything to the last minute
Ignoring your own health and rest

questions.expected: All six habits sorted good vs poor (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Good self-management: punctual, calm, professional. Poor self-management: procrastinating, neglecting health, blaming others.

questions.question: A learner says: 'Self-management just means doing whatever the supervisor tells me.' How should this be corrected?
options: Self-management is taking charge of yourself without being told; following orders is being managed by others
She is right, it means obeying orders
Self-management means ignoring the supervisor completely
Self-management has nothing to do with work
questions.expected: Self-management is taking charge of yourself without being told; following orders is being managed by others
questions.memo: Don't confuse the two: managing yourself is doing the right things on your own initiative, not simply obeying instructions.

questions.question: Why is self-management often called the foundation for managing other people?
options: If you can reliably manage your own time, goals and behaviour, you can be trusted to manage others
Because managing others requires no skills at all
Because self-management replaces the need for any managers
questions.expected: If you can reliably manage your own time, goals and behaviour, you can be trusted to manage others
questions.memo: You must master managing yourself first; that reliability is what earns the trust and skill to manage other people.

questions.question: How do strong self-management skills help a person succeed at work?
options: They make the person reliable, productive and able to cope with pressure and change
They make the person dependent on constant supervision
They have no effect on the person's work
They guarantee the person never has to learn anything
questions.expected: They make the person reliable, productive and able to cope with pressure and change
questions.memo: Self-management makes someone dependable and productive, and helps them handle stress and change — all of which support success.

questions.question: Match each action to the self-management skill it shows.

items.text: Making a daily schedule and sticking to it
Taking deep breaths before a big presentation
Dressing neatly and speaking politely at work
Prioritising the most urgent tasks first
Going for a walk to clear your head

questions.expected: All six actions matched to the right skill (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Scheduling and prioritising = time management; staying calm = stress management; dressing and behaving well = professional image.

BUS.G10.T4.TEAM.A1.title: Relationships & team performance
BUS.G10.T4.TEAM.A1.description: How people work together to reach business goals, the factors that affect workplace relationships (prejudice, beliefs, values, diversity), and the criteria for successful, collaborative team performance — kept apart from the barriers to it.
BUS.G10.T4.TEAM.A1.recovery_strategy: Good teams share: clear goals, openness, mutual respect and trust, commitment, sound relations. Barriers are the opposite: prejudice, poor communication, distrust. Diversity is a strength when managed well.

questions.question: What is a team in a business?
options: A group of people working together towards a shared goal
A list of the business's customers
questions.expected: A group of people working together towards a shared goal
questions.memo: A team is people working together towards a shared goal, combining their efforts and skills.

questions.question: True or false: Mutual respect and trust help a team perform well.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Respect and trust are key criteria for good teamwork — they reduce conflict and help members work together.

questions.question: Clear, shared _________ are a key criterion for good teamwork.
questions.expected: goals
questions.memo: A good team shares clear goals, so everyone is pulling in the same direction.

questions.question: Which of these is a criterion for successful teamwork?
questions.expected: Open communication between members
questions.memo: Open communication is a criterion for good teamwork. The others are barriers that harm a team.

questions.question: True or false: Prejudice is a criterion for good teamwork.
questions.expected: False
questions.memo: False — prejudice is a barrier, not a criterion. Good teamwork needs respect, trust and openness.

questions.question: When team members judge others unfairly because of their background, this is called _________.
questions.expected: prejudice
questions.memo: Prejudice is judging people unfairly because of their background — a barrier to good workplace relationships.

questions.question: Which pair correctly shows one thing that HELPS a team and one that HARMS it?
questions.expected: Mutual respect helps; distrust harms
questions.memo: Respect helps a team; distrust harms it. Keep the helpers (criteria) apart from the harmers (barriers).

questions.question: How can diversity strengthen a team when it is managed well?
options: Different backgrounds bring a wider range of skills, ideas and viewpoints
It guarantees the team will always argue
It makes everyone think exactly alike
It removes the need for any goals
questions.expected: Different backgrounds bring a wider range of skills, ideas and viewpoints
questions.memo: Well-managed diversity is a strength: varied backgrounds add more skills, ideas and perspectives to the team.

questions.question: Sort each factor by whether it helps or harms teamwork.
questions.expected: All six factors sorted helps vs harms (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Communication, trust, respect and commitment help a team. Prejudice, secrecy and distrust harm it.

questions.question: What happens to a team when communication is poor?
options: Misunderstandings, mistakes and conflict become more likely
questions.expected: Misunderstandings, mistakes and conflict become more likely
questions.memo: Poor communication leads to misunderstandings, errors and conflict — it is a barrier to good team performance.

questions.question: Thesis: 'Good teamwork improves a business's performance.' Choose the THREE strongest supporting reasons.
questions.thesis: Good teamwork improves a business's performance.

pool.text: Members share ideas and skills, so problems are solved faster
Trust and respect reduce conflict and wasted time
Clear shared goals keep everyone pulling in the same direction
Teams always work slower than one person alone
The team happens to meet in a room with blue walls
Teamwork only matters at the year-end party

questions.memo: Shared skills, trust and clear goals all lift performance. The 'slower than one person' point is a counter, the blue walls are irrelevant, and 'only at the party' is weak.

questions.question: A team works best when its members are _________ to the shared goal.
questions.expected: committed
questions.memo: Commitment — members genuinely caring about the shared goal — is a key criterion for strong teamwork.

questions.question: Two team members hold different personal beliefs. What is the best way to handle this for good teamwork?
options: Respect each other's differences and focus on the shared goal
Mock the beliefs they disagree with
Exclude one member from the team
Refuse to work with anyone different
questions.expected: Respect each other's differences and focus on the shared goal
questions.memo: Differences in beliefs and values are handled well through respect — keeping the focus on the shared goal.

questions.question: True or false: Diversity in a team is always a weakness.
questions.expected: False
questions.memo: False — diversity is a strength when managed well, bringing more skills and ideas. Only poorly handled differences cause problems.

questions.question: Which of these is a BARRIER to good teamwork?
questions.expected: Distrust between members
questions.memo: Distrust is a barrier that harms a team. Clear goals, communication and respect are criteria that help it.

questions.question: Sort each item as a criterion for good teamwork or a barrier to it.
questions.expected: All six items sorted criterion vs barrier (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Criteria are the things good teams share (clear goals, respect, commitment). Barriers are the opposite (poor communication, prejudice, distrust).

questions.question: Thesis: 'A diverse team can be a strength for a business.' Choose the THREE strongest reasons.
questions.thesis: A diverse team can be a strength for a business.

pool.text: Different backgrounds bring a wider range of ideas and skills
Members can understand and serve a wider range of customers
Varied viewpoints help the team avoid blind spots
Differences always cause arguments that ruin teams
The team's logo is green
Diversity only counts on public holidays

questions.memo: Diversity adds ideas and skills, helps the team understand more customers, and reduces blind spots. The 'always argues' point is a counter, the logo is irrelevant, and 'only on holidays' is weak.

questions.question: A learner lists 'prejudice' as a criterion for successful teamwork. How should this be corrected?
options: Prejudice is a barrier, not a criterion; good teamwork needs respect, trust and openness
She is right, prejudice builds strong teams
Prejudice has no effect on teams
Prejudice is the most important criterion
questions.expected: Prejudice is a barrier, not a criterion; good teamwork needs respect, trust and openness
questions.memo: Don't confuse the two: prejudice harms a team (a barrier). The criteria for good teamwork are respect, trust, openness and shared goals.

questions.question: Why is mutual trust so important for collaboration in a team?
options: When members trust each other they share openly, rely on one another and work towards the goal without fear
Trust makes members compete against each other
Trust removes the need for any communication
Trust means no one has to do any work
questions.expected: When members trust each other they share openly, rely on one another and work towards the goal without fear
questions.memo: Trust is the glue of collaboration: it lets members share honestly and depend on one another to reach the goal.

questions.question: Sort each behaviour as good team behaviour or a barrier to teamwork.

items.text: Listening to a teammate's idea respectfully
Excluding someone because of their background

questions.expected: All six behaviours sorted correctly (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Good team behaviour builds trust and shares the load. Barriers exclude people, hide information and refuse to cooperate.
